title: Life Plan Residents' Reduction on Missed Visit Hours — Personal Services Plan
content:
Residents of the Life Plan campuses who hold an Entrance Fee Agreement owe fewer hours when a Personal Services Plan visit is cancelled late or missed.

## Rule

The entrance reduction is 0.20 hour where the resident whose visit was missed holds an occupied Entrance Fee Agreement on a lifecare contract (the LifeCare Declining Balance Plan or the LifeCare 90% Refundable Plan), 0.10 hour where the resident holds an occupied Entrance Fee Agreement on a fee-for-service contract (any LifeChoice plan), and nothing otherwise.

The reduction is subtracted from the hours owed for the missed visit after every multiplication of those hours has been made; the remainder is never below zero and is rounded to two decimal places half up only after the subtraction.

The test reads the resident's Entrance Fee Agreement records: whether an agreement is recorded as occupied, and its contract type — lifecare for the LifeCare Declining Balance Plan and the LifeCare 90% Refundable Plan, fee-for-service for any LifeChoice plan.

## Ladder

| Resident's Entrance Fee Agreement | Reduction |
|---|---|
| Occupied, lifecare contract | 0.20 hour |
| Occupied, fee-for-service contract | 0.10 hour |
| Not occupied, or none held | Nothing |

## Hypothetical cases

- Hours owed of 1.0 before the reduction, lifecare contract: 1.0 less 0.20, or 0.80 hour.
- Hours owed of 0.25 before the reduction, fee-for-service contract: 0.25 less 0.10, or 0.15 hour.
- Hours owed of 0.15 before the reduction, lifecare contract: 0.15 less 0.20 would fall below zero, so the hours owed are 0.00.
